newsitem.title: USA: Pulitzer sees tough revenue comparisons.
newsitem.headline: Pulitzer sees tough revenue comparisons.

text.p: Pulitzer Publishing Co said Wednesday it expects 1997 revenues to face tough comparisons with 1996 levels.

"That's particularly true on the broadcasting side, since we experienced substantial political spending and advertising in connection with the Summer Olympics in the second half of 1996," chief executive officer Michael Pulitzer said in a news release.
Earlier Wednesday, Pulitzer reported net income of $12.5 million or $0.57 a share for the first quarter, compared to $10.2 million or $0.47 a share a year ago.

Publishing cash flow increased to $14.5 million from $5.9 million while broadcasting cash flow increased to $20.7 million from $20.6 million, Pulitzer said. Publishing cash flow was boosted in 1997 by the acquisition of Scripps League Newspapers Inc.
Lower newsprint expenses and increased advertising revenue boosted percomance in the media companies publishing segment.
